title: Creamy Garlic Tuscan Chicken (One-Pan 30-Minute Dinner)
contentHtml:
This creamy garlic Tuscan chicken is the kind of dinner that looks restaurant-level but is still realistic on a weeknight. Four golden chicken breasts simmer in a garlic-Parmesan cream sauce with spinach and sun-dried tomatoes, all in one skillet.

Servings: 4  |  Prep: 10 minutes  |  Cook: 20 minutes  |  Total: about 30 minutes

Why This One Works

  • One skillet: less cleanup and all the browned chicken flavor stays in the sauce.
  • Fast: the whole thing can be on the table in about 30 minutes.
  • Big flavor: garlic, Parmesan and sun-dried tomatoes do the heavy lifting.
  • Easy to pair: serve it over pasta, rice, mashed potatoes, or with crusty bread.

Ingredients

  • 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, about 6 ounces each
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt, divided
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1/2 cup sun-dried tomatoes, drained and sliced
  • 1 cup low-sodium chicken broth
  • 1 cup heavy cream
  • 1/2 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese
  • 2 packed cups fresh baby spinach
  • 1 tablespoon chopped fresh basil or parsley, optional

Instructions

  1. Season the chicken. Pat the chicken dry. Season both sides with 3/4 teaspoon salt, black pepper and Italian seasoning.
  2. Sear it. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook for about 4 to 5 minutes per side until deeply golden. Transfer it to a plate. It does not have to be completely cooked yet.
  3. Build the flavor. Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic and sun-dried tomatoes to the same skillet and cook for about 30 seconds, stirring so the garlic does not burn.
  4. Make the sauce. Pour in the chicken broth and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. Stir in the heavy cream and bring it to a gentle simmer.
  5. Add Parmesan and spinach. Stir in the Parmesan until melted, then add the spinach a handful at a time until wilted. Taste the sauce and add the remaining salt if needed.
  6. Finish the chicken. Return the chicken and any juices to the skillet. Simmer gently for 4 to 6 minutes, spooning sauce over the top, until the thickest part of each breast reaches 165°F.
  7. Serve. Spoon plenty of the spinach, sun-dried tomatoes and cream sauce over each chicken breast. Finish with basil or parsley if you have it.

Dad-Proof Tips

  • If your chicken breasts are really thick, slice them horizontally into thinner cutlets before cooking. It speeds everything up and prevents the outside from burning while the middle catches up.
  • Do not crank the heat after adding the cream. A gentle simmer gives you a smooth sauce.
  • Freshly grated Parmesan melts better than the shelf-stable shaker kind.
  • The instant-read thermometer wins again. Pull the chicken when it hits 165°F instead of cutting every piece open to check.

What to Serve With It

Pasta is the obvious move because that sauce deserves somewhere to go, but rice, mashed potatoes, roasted potatoes, or warm crusty bread all work. Add a simple salad if you want to pretend this was a carefully planned restaurant dinner.

Storage and Reheating

Store leftovers in a covered container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently over low heat or in short microwave intervals. If the sauce gets too thick, stir in a splash of chicken broth or milk.

This is an original The Man That Cooks Sometimes recipe built for a night when you want something that looks impressive without turning dinner into a project.
